result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=with, B=without): Both answers cover the same core points well: matched Devanagari and Latin faces, Hindi set 10–15% larger with more line height, tabular Western digits used throughout, and fonts embedded with a print proof and a phone check. B is more useful in practice. It works out how much the A3 layout shrinks on a phone, gives a concrete phone layout, and adds tagging, language marking and contrast checks. A is a little more explicit that a mismatched fallback font is the usual failure, and it asks for one consistent time format. | pass 2 (A=without, B=with): Both answers give a concrete size order with point sizes, match Hindi size and line height to the English, and cover embedding and proofing. B is slightly stronger: it warns more directly against letting an unmatched fallback font fill in the Devanagari, and it handles times more fully (tabular figures plus one consistent 24-hour or am/pm format). A's best extra is a sharper analysis of A3-to-phone scaling, but neither answer explicitly says a Latin-only font will show missing glyphs.
